insights: Shopping, leisure, and pick-up trips show greater motor-vehicle reliance than education trips.
Trips for pick-up sustain relatively longer distances than other usages, but a few outliers with very long durations exist.
Education trips are concentrated in fixed morning and afternoon windows, whereas the other usages are more dispersed across the afternoon and evening.
summary: Shopping, leisure, and pick-up trips have greater motor-vehicle reliance than education trips. Pick-up trips are relatively longer, with a small set of long-duration records forming the upper duration tail. Education trips occur in fixed morning and afternoon windows, whereas the other usages are more dispersed across the afternoon and evening.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
